question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Catarina Vieira (Verts/ALE), Marit Maij (S&D), Nela Riehl (Verts/ALE), JanChristoph Oetjen (Renew) Subject:

In addition to evidence of the role of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in providing weapons and military equipment to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan, several credible sources1, including a recent Human Rights Watch (HRW) report2, have reported that UAEbased businesses are involved in hiring and transporting Colombian private military contractors. HRW documented their transit via UAE military facilities and presence in ElFasher, during which these forces conducted a campaign which bore ‘hallmarks of genocide’3. 1.

Has the European External Action Service (EEAS) documented the role of UAE-based company Global Security Services Group (GSSG) and its CEO Mohamed Hamdan alZaabi and other entities in hiring and transporting foreign fighters to support the RSF, with a view to proposing to the Council their listing under its Sudan sanction regime?

What is the EEAS and Commission’s assessment of the UAE’s or UAE-based entities’ role in the provision of weapons and military equipment4 to the RSF – including Bulgarian-made ammunitions5 and French-made equipment6?

Has the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy assessed whether the UAE’s actions are in breach of criteria under the EU Common Position 2008/944/CFSP with a view to proposing an EU arms embargo on the UAE or any other appropriate action?

https://thesentry.org/reports/sudan-mercenaries-rsf-uae-bureaucrat/. https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/05/25/from-bogota-to-el-fasher/the-uaes-role-in-the-deployment-ofcolombian-fighters. 3 https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/thematic-reports/ahrc6177-sudan-hallmarks-genocide-el-fasherreport-independent. 4 provision of weapons and military equipment. 5 https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20250417-investigation-european-weapons-sudan-part-1-mortarshells-bulgaria. 6 https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/sudan-french-manufactured-weapons-systemidentified-in-conflict-new-investigation/. 1 2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.8.2026) The EU has reiterated on multiple occasions that the primary responsibility for ending the conflict in Sudan lies with the leadership of both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), and those supporting these entities. The EU has addressed the situation in Sudan during its political dialogues and exchanges with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) at various levels. The EU has raised concerns about the reported UAE support to the RSF and will continue engaging with the UAE, which is a member of the Quad (together with United States of America, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Egypt) on Sudan, to reach a sustainable ceasefire and a peaceful resolution of the conflict. Enhanced political dialogue is a key tenet of the future Strategic Partnership Agreement, reflecting the shared commitment to promoting regional stability and prosperity. The EU is closely monitoring the actions of all parties to the conflict. The High Representative/Vice President will continue to engage with Member States on the available options under the EU restrictive measures (sanctions). The EU has urged all external actors to take necessary measures to end the sale or supply of arms and related material to all parties as per the arms embargo established by the UN Security Council Resolutions 1556 (2004) and 1591 (2005). The EU has transposed the UN embargo by prohibiting the sale, supply, transfer or export of arms and related materiel of all types to the entire territory of Sudan. The implementation is the responsibility of Member States. In the Council Conclusions on Sudan of October 2025, the EU urged all external actors directly or indirectly supplying arms, financial support or support of any other kind to the warring parties to immediately cease such support1.
